message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for residential units; two months for furnished units.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize any deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, structural integrity).
• Must repair major defects promptly. | If landlord fails to fix serious problems, tenants may withhold rent or pursue repairs themselves and recover costs. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without proper notice (usually 24‑hour written notice unless emergency).
• Landlord must respect your right to privacy. | Exceptions: emergencies, repairs, inspections with notice, or if lease allows otherwise. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination, landlord must give at least 90 days’ written notice for month‑to‑month leases.
• For lease termination due to violation, notice period depends on the nature of the violation. | Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or handicap. | Also protected under federal Fair Housing Act. | | **Repair and Deduct / Rent Escrow** | • If landlord fails to make necessary repairs, tenants may pay the cost themselves and deduct from rent, or place rent in escrow. | Must follow proper procedure: notify landlord, allow reasonable time to repair, keep receipts. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for leases longer than one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) are enforceable only if they comply with local ordinances. | Some localities have stricter rules (e.g., city ordinances banning “no pets” clauses). | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease violations).
• Eviction must proceed through court; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | Tenants can contest eviction in court; courts often require proof of notice and documentation. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified in lease. | Lease may specify which utilities are tenant’s responsibility. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Tenants may sublet or assign lease with landlord’s consent, unless lease prohibits it. | Consent must be in writing; some leases restrict subletting but still require landlord approval. | ### Practical Steps If You Encounter Issues 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, photos of damage, receipts for repairs, etc. 2. **Written Notice** – Send any complaints or requests in writing (email or certified mail) so there’s a record. 3. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If disputes arise, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid organization. --- #### Quick Reference: How to File a Complaint | Issue | Where to File | Contact Info | |-------|---------------|--------------| | Discrimination | U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) | https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp | | Unlawful Eviction | Texas Attorney General’s Office | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/ | | Local Housing Complaints | City or County Housing Agency | Check your city’s official website for contact details. | If you need a specific clause drafted for a lease or a formal complaint letter, let me know and I can help draft that.
